quiz.where: Final test vs goals (goals lines 14-17; tests lines 293-399)
quiz.problem: Two goals aren't fully covered by the Final test. Goal 3 promises "what earns a place in a steering file", but only the globality Checkpoint tests that; predict-stale-init covers only the /init half. Goal 4 lists six ideas, and the Final test checks just two of them (context pointers in predict-weak-pointer, positive phrasing in spot-negation). The two loads, progressive disclosure, leading words and no-ops never appear in the Final test. Goal 2's "a pointer for slow searching" home is also never tested in a /retro situation.
quiz.evidence: The 9 tests: repeat-mistake (check), style-drift (standards), cleared-session (timing), which-skill, negation, automated-retro, stale-init, weak-pointer, sequence. None asks which line earns a place in CLAUDE.md, and none covers progressive disclosure, the two loads or leading words.
quiz.fix:
Add a 10th test (allowed range 8-10), with the right answer in position a (a is currently used only once):
```test scenario-earns-a-line
You're pruning a teammate's `CLAUDE.md`. Which line earns its place?
- [x] "Payments: read docs/payments.md before touching checkout code."
  > Right. It's a navigation pointer with a clear trigger, the main thing a steering file is for.
- [ ] "This project is a Next.js app written in TypeScript with Tailwind."
  > The config files already say so. A copy of something discoverable costs every session and goes stale.
- [ ] "Run `npm test` before every commit to run the whole test suite."
  > That's mechanical: a pre-commit hook enforces it, and a sentence can't fail.
- [ ] "Always write well-tested, maintainable and readable code."
  > A no-op. It doesn't change what the agent does by default.
```
(Check the lengths with lint: the right option is about 63 characters, the others 64-67.) Then either narrow goal 4 to "...with `/writing-for-agents`: sharpen context pointers, cut no-ops and state the positive", or swap one question for a progressive-disclosure item, for example: "Your 600-line migration Skill covers Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, but each project uses one, and runs skip steps near the top. What does `/writing-for-agents` suggest?" Right answer: "Keep shared steps inline; move per-database notes to linked files." Distractors: bold every step; paste it all into `CLAUDE.md`; ask the agent to streamline the file to half its length.

quiz.problem: This tests recall, not transfer. The prompt reuses the body's own example word for word ("Don't write long comments"), and the right option's feedback repeats the body's fix ("Keep every comment to one line"). The writing guide says to use a fresh situation, not the body's example.
quiz.evidence: Body line 176: "\"Don't write long comments\" puts long comments front and centre; \"Keep every comment to one line\" never mentions them." Test prompt: "Dana added \"Don't write long comments.\" to `CLAUDE.md`."
quiz.fix: Use a fresh case that is a judgement call, not something a lint rule could catch (otherwise "make it a check" becomes a second right answer): "After the agent kept writing error messages full of developer jargon, Dana added \"Don't use technical jargon in error messages.\" to `CLAUDE.md`. Now the messages mention stack traces and status codes even more. Spot the mistake." Right option b: "The ban names the unwanted behaviour instead of the wanted one." Feedback: "Right. Negation keeps jargon in the agent's attention. 'Write every error message in words a Visitor would use' states the target instead." Keep options a, c and d as they are, with "long comments" in option a's feedback changed to "jargon".

quiz.problem: This also tests recall, not transfer. "The wrong package manager" is the body's own example of a mechanical slip three times over (Why it matters, the mechanical paragraph, and the flow Scene caption), so a reader can match the phrase without applying the mechanical-or-judgement test.
quiz.evidence: Line 22: "It runs `npm install` in a project that uses a different package manager." Line 55: "...the wrong package manager." Scene caption, line 71: "A fixed pattern, like the wrong package manager, gets a check that fails".
quiz.fix: Use a fresh mechanical slip from SKILL.md's "banned API / import shape" class: "On a recipe site, the agent keeps importing dates from `moment`, a library the team removed months ago. The reviewer has caught it in three PRs running. You run `/retro`. Which proposal fits how it sorts problems?" Options: a "A new line in `CLAUDE.md`: 'Never import moment.'"; b "A rule in `CODING_STANDARDS.md` for the reviewer agent to enforce." (feedback: "Standards are for judgement calls. A banned import is a fixed pattern a tool can catch."); c [x] "A lint rule that fails whenever `moment` is imported." (feedback: "Right. It's mechanical, so it gets a deterministic check that runs in a pre-commit hook or CI job."); d the memory-note option, unchanged. In d's feedback, also change "so the mistake can't happen again" to "so the mistake gets caught next time": a check catches a slip, it doesn't prevent it.
